bullets.text: ML is a subfield of Artificial Intelligence (AI) focused on systems learning from data.
Models learn patterns from data to make decisions or predictions, rather than fixed rules.
ML models improve over time with more data without needing reprogramming.
It's about teaching computers to learn from experience, similar to humans.

sections.heading: Importance and Growth of Machine Learning

bullets.text: ML is ubiquitous: powers Netflix recommendations, spam filters, virtual assistants, and fraud detection.
Its popularity is due to access to vast amounts of data.
Enabled by increased computational power, especially modern GPUs.
Development of sophisticated algorithms for extracting insights.
Most common type, trains models using labeled data (input + correct output).
Goal is for the model to predict outputs for new, unseen inputs.
Example: predicting house prices based on features and historical sale prices.
Problems split into Regression (predicting continuous values) and Classification (predicting discrete labels).
Uses unlabeled data; algorithms discover patterns, relationships, or structures on their own.
Common application is Clustering, grouping similar data points.
Example: grouping customers by buying behavior for targeted marketing.
Also includes Dimensionality Reduction to simplify datasets with many features.
An agent learns by interacting with an environment.
Receives feedback as rewards or penalties for its decisions.
Goal: learn a policy to maximize total reward over time.
Examples: training robots to walk, game-playing AI like AlphaGo, self-driving cars.
Data quality is crucial; noisy, biased, or incomplete data harms model performance.
Overfitting occurs when a model learns training data too well but fails on new data.
Ethical concerns are prominent, as biased data can lead to biased models with serious consequences.
Understanding data, context, and real-world impact is as important as algorithms.
Recap: Covered ML definition, importance, three main types, and challenges.
Future lectures will delve deeper into specific algorithms and practical applications.
